rows.label: V1 lab (Josh: 'close')
rows.quitText: So I'm planting the flag. Miami is the overwhelming ACC favorite as long as Mensah is upright. Clemson on October 3 is the result that makes me reopen it.
smell: Because the calendar is doing more work here than the roster gap is.
That is the one result that reopens this race.
Miami can lose in South Bend and wake up the next morning exactly as much the conference favorite as it was at kickoff.
If SMU is going to be the answer to "then who," it has to bank Florida State and Louisville before Miami ever plays a real league game.
Clemson on October 3 is the result that makes me reopen it.

rows.label: V1 production
rows.quitText: And I'll be honest about the shape of my own case, because it isn't airtight. This is an argument by elimination, which is the cheapest way to win one. I have not taken SMU apart position by position on this show. I have not built a case against Louisville. I looked at the alternatives, none of them got past a Miami roster that opens seventh in the country, and that was the end of my thinking. Clemson at least has the date, the home crowd, and a real chance to take the words "by far" out of my mouth. If SMU or Louisville makes me look slow in September, good. I'll say so on the air.
smell: The schedule is what turns a favorite into an overwhelming one.
The conference gets decided in Clemson and in the games nobody is buying tickets to yet.
Best team in the ACC and winner of the ACC are two separate bets, and the popular take sells you the second one at the price of the first.

It gives one other program in this conference a head-to-head result over Miami, which is the only currency that converts a coronation into a race, and it makes every Miami Saturday after it read differently.
The grade on this one comes the night the ACC championship game produces a winner, and if the program standing there isn't Miami, I'll print that miss myself before anybody else gets the chance to.

rows.label: V2 (loop 4)
rows.quitText: The Clemson objection is the easy one to state: my own board has them ahead of the team I keep calling the runaway ACC favorite, so why exactly am I waving them off as an alternative? I don't have a tidy answer beyond the fact that a national ranking and a conference favorite tag are answering slightly different questions, and that Clemson's finished 2025 record is the only thing either of us can actually point to.
smell: That is the first date on Miami's schedule where a broad opinion about the ACC has to become a result, and it happens to involve one of the three teams I named out loud as the only realistic alternatives to Miami.

rows.label: D · Josh's hand edit
rows.quitText: And understand what October 3 actually decides, because it is more than one line in the loss column. It is the head-to-head result that settles any tiebreaker between the league's two most talented rosters. It is Miami's lone trip to a ranked conference opponent, in a venue that has ended more favorite runs than any other stop in this league. And it is the one Saturday all season when the rest of the ACC gets to find out, in real time, whether the twelve-spot gap is a fact or a projection. Win in Death Valley and the conversation about the ACC race is functionally over in the first week of October.
